candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate just culture from both punitive and accountability-free approaches.

options.A: Every error is punished the same way regardless of the behavior involved.
options.B: Human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless behavior are distinguished so the response can address both system factors and appropriate accountability.
options.C: No staff member is ever accountable for any unsafe behavior.
options.D: Only the severity of the patient outcome determines whether staff are disciplined.

candidate.rationale: A just culture balances learning from system failures with accountability for behavior. AHRQ distinguishes human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless behavior and supports different responses rather than treating all errors as blame-free or punishing every event identically.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Just culture differentiates behavior types and applies proportionate responses while examining system contributors.
candidate.source_locator: Just culture—distinguishes human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless behavior; balances systems learning and accountability
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, PSNet
candidate.stem: Which statement best describes a just culture approach after a patient-safety event?
